title: Collaboration and co-creation
blurb: Define co-creation as PRINCE2 7 does, tell it apart from wider collaboration, and explain how it builds ownership and adoption.
question: A supplier wants to build a new booking system to its own design and show it to users at handover. What would PRINCE2's idea of co-creation recommend instead?

teach.body: Collaboration is people across the project ecosystem working together towards the project's objectives. Formally, co-creation is a specific form of collaboration: it involves users and key influencers in designing products and agreed ways of working, so that they are adopted by the project and organizational ecosystems. In plain English: do not build it for people and hand it over; build it with them so they own it.

rows.label: What
values: Designing products and ways of working

teach.body: A project only succeeds when its products are used. Co-creating products with the business, user and supplier communities, against agreed product descriptions, unites their different perspectives. That improves both how the products are developed and how they are adopted, reduces handover risks, and makes sure operational and maintenance needs are considered. Co-creating ways of working also makes people more willing to be managed in line with them.

teach.caption: This is how the people element applies the focus on products principle (manual 3.5.1).

teach.h: Where co-creation shows up in PRINCE2
head: What is co-created
Who with
rows: Project manager with the team manager
teach.caption: Work packages are co-created and reviewed in 'controlling a stage' before authorization; the delivering level co-creates where required.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Kestrel Valley Health Trust
teach.body: Kestrel Valley's first attempt at a digital discharge checklist was designed by the IT team alone; ward nurses kept using paper. On the new project, project manager Amara Okafor sets up design sessions with ward nurses (users), the chief pharmacist (a key influencer) and the software supplier. Together they agree the product description, test drafts on two wards and plan how the checklist will be supported after go-live. Nurses now call it 'our checklist'.

children.edge: Users or key influencers help design
children.label: Co-creation
children.sub: of products or agreed ways of working

children.label: Collaboration
children.sub: the wider idea that includes co-creation

teach.text: Co-creation is not showing users a finished product and asking for sign-off, and it does not move accountability. The project manager still authorizes the work package, the senior supplier is still accountable for supplier quality and the board still directs. Co-creation changes how things are designed, not who is accountable.

items: Co-creation is a specific form of collaboration involving users and key influencers in designing products and agreed ways of working (manual 3.3).
Its aim is adoption by the project and organizational ecosystems.
Co-creating products with business, user and supplier communities improves development and adoption and reduces handover risks (manual 3.5.1).
Co-created ways of working make people more willing to be managed in line with them.
The project manager co-creates each work package with the team manager before authorizing it.

summary: You can now define co-creation as the form of collaboration that brings users and key influencers into designing products and ways of working, and explain why it improves adoption and reduces handover risk. You can also spot where PRINCE2 expects it, from product descriptions to work packages.

A.q: Which statement best describes co-creation in PRINCE2 7?
options: Joint working between the project manager and the board on stage plans
Involving users and key influencers in designing products and ways of working
Agreeing a contract with a supplier that shares the delivery risk
Reviewing finished products with users before handover is accepted
A.why: Co-creation is a specific form of collaboration involving users and key influencers in designing products and agreed ways of working (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Planning between the project manager and the board is part of the plans practice and directing, not the definition of co-creation.
whyNot.2: Contract and risk-sharing arrangements belong to the commercial management approach.
whyNot.3: Reviewing finished products is acceptance; co-creation involves people in the design, not only at the end.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Co-creation is a specific form of [?] in which users and key influencers help design products and agreed ways of working.
options: consultation
delegation
assurance
collaboration
A.why: PRINCE2 describes co-creation as a specific form of collaboration (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Consultation asks for views; co-creation is described as a form of collaboration in which people design together.
whyNot.1: Delegation passes authority down the levels of organization; it is a different idea.
whyNot.2: Assurance is the independent checking of the project on behalf of the board.

A.q: According to PRINCE2, what is the aim of involving users and key influencers in designing products and ways of working?
options: Their adoption by the project and organizational ecosystems
A reduction in the number of management stages needed
A transfer of accountability from the executive to users
Removing the need to write product descriptions
A.why: Co-creation is intended to ensure products and ways of working are adopted by the project and organizational ecosystems (manual 3.3).

whyNot.1: The number of stages depends on risk, decision points and planning horizon, not on co-creation.
whyNot.2: The executive remains the single point of accountability; co-creation does not change that.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 links co-creation to agreed product descriptions; they are still written.

B.q:
Which two statements about co-creation are correct?
1. It involves users and key influencers in designing products.
2. It replaces the need for agreed product descriptions.
3. It helps ensure operational and maintenance needs are considered.
4. It is carried out by the project board on behalf of users.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: Co-creation involves users and key influencers in design (1) and, by uniting perspectives, helps ensure operational and maintenance needs are considered (3) (manual 3.3, 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: co-creation works with agreed product descriptions rather than replacing them.
whyNot.1: Both are false: product descriptions are still agreed, and co-creation involves users directly rather than the board acting for them.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the point is to involve users and key influencers themselves.

B.q: In 'controlling a stage', how should the project manager arrive at a work package with a team manager?
options: Co-create it with the team manager, then authorize it
Draft it in full and send it to the team manager to execute
Ask the project board to agree it with the team manager
Let the team manager write and authorize it themselves
B.why: The project manager co-creates and reviews the work package with the team manager, confirms acceptance and then authorizes the work (manual 16.4.1).

whyNot.1: Drafting it in full without the team manager loses the team manager's ownership; PRINCE2 expects the work package to be co-created.
whyNot.2: The board is not involved in agreeing work packages; that sits between the project manager and team manager.
whyNot.3: The team manager agrees and accepts the work package, but the project manager authorizes it.

B.q: A software supplier proposes building a booking system to its own design and showing it to users at handover. What does PRINCE2's view of co-creation suggest?
options: It is sound, as the supplier is accountable for product quality
Users should sign off the design after the build has finished
The executive should design it to protect the business case
Users should help design it, improving adoption and handover
B.why: Co-creating products with users unites perspectives, improves adoption and reduces handover risks (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: The senior supplier is accountable for supplier quality, but that does not explain why users should be left out of the design.
whyNot.1: Sign-off at the end is acceptance, not co-creation; users need to be involved in the design itself.
whyNot.2: The executive owns the business case; designing products with users is what improves adoption.

C.q: Which principle is the people element applying when business, user and supplier communities co-create products against agreed product descriptions?
options: Manage by exception
Focus on products
Learn from experience
Manage by stages
C.why: PRINCE2 links co-creating products, with agreed product descriptions, to the focus on products principle (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Manage by exception in the people element is about deciding at the most local level where the knowledge resides.
whyNot.2: Learn from experience in the people element is about social learning and sharing hidden knowledge.
whyNot.3: Manage by stages in the people element is about stages marking changes in influencers and key relationships.

C.q: A project team co-created its reporting routines with team members and key stakeholders. Which effect does PRINCE2 associate with this?
options: The board no longer needs highlight reports from the PM
Team managers become accountable for the business case
People are more willing to be managed in line with them
The PM no longer needs to set work package tolerances
C.why: Co-creating ways of working with team members and stakeholders significantly improves people's willingness to be managed in line with them (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Highlight reports are still produced at the frequency set in the communication management approach.
whyNot.1: The executive owns the business case; co-creation does not change accountability.
whyNot.3: Work package tolerances are still set by the project manager to enable management by exception.

C.q: During delivery, a team manager works with the warehouse staff who will use a new picking system to shape how it works. Which level of organization is this, and what is happening?
options: Delivering level; co-creating with others in the project ecosystem
Directing level; project assurance carried out for the senior user
Managing level; quality assurance of the picking system
Business layer; commissioning the project's products
C.why: Team managers sit at the delivering level and co-create where required with others from across the project ecosystem; involving users in design is co-creation.

whyNot.1: A team manager is not at the directing level, and shaping the product with users is not assurance.
whyNot.2: Quality assurance is an independent business function outside the project management team.
whyNot.3: The business layer sits outside the project and commissions it; it does not shape products with users during delivery.

reteach.title: Planning a kitchen with the cook
reteach.question: Why would a builder plan a new kitchen with the person who cooks in it every day?

blocks.body: A builder could fit a beautiful kitchen from a catalogue and hand over the keys. But the person who cooks daily knows where the bins must go, which shelves get used and how the room is cleaned. Planning together unites both views, the kitchen gets used as intended and nothing has to be ripped out after handover. That is co-creation.

blocks.text: The builder is still responsible for building it properly. Co-creation shares the design, not the accountability.

explain.body: Co-creation involves users and key influencers in designing products and agreed ways of working, so they are adopted by the project and organizational ecosystems.

test.q: Who does co-creation specifically involve in designing products and ways of working?
options: Project support and the project manager
The business layer and the executive
Quality assurance and internal audit
Users and key influencers
test.why: Co-creation involves users and key influencers in design (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Project support provides administrative services; co-creation is about involving users and key influencers.
whyNot.1: The business layer commissions the project; co-creation brings in users and key influencers.
whyNot.2: Quality assurance is independent of the project management team and checks rather than designs.

explain.body: Co-creating products with business, user and supplier communities unites their perspectives, improves development and adoption, reduces handover risks and makes sure operational and maintenance needs are considered.

test.q: Which outcome does PRINCE2 link to co-creating products with business, user and supplier communities?
options: Fewer quality reviews for each product
Reduced handover risks into the business
Shorter management stages throughout
Narrower tolerances on project cost
test.why: Co-creation improves development and adoption and reduces handover risks (manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Quality reviews are set by the quality management approach and product descriptions, not reduced by co-creation.
whyNot.2: Stage length depends on risk and decision points.
whyNot.3: Cost tolerances are set by the board and project manager under manage by exception.

explain.body: In 'controlling a stage' the project manager builds a working relationship with the team manager, co-creates and reviews the work package with them, confirms they accept it and then authorizes the work.

test.q: Which management product does the project manager co-create with a team manager before authorizing work?
options: End stage report
Highlight report
Work package
Lessons report
test.why: The work package (its description) is co-created and reviewed with the team manager in 'controlling a stage' (manual 16.4.1).

whyNot.0: The end stage report is produced by the project manager for the board at the end of a stage.
whyNot.1: The highlight report goes from the project manager to the board on stage status.
whyNot.3: The lessons report passes lessons on; it is not agreed with a team manager to start work.

explain.body: Collaboration is the wider idea of working together across the project ecosystem. Co-creation is one specific form of it, focused on designing products and ways of working with users and key influencers.

test.q: Which statement about collaboration and co-creation is correct?
options: Co-creation is a specific form of collaboration
Collaboration is a specific form of co-creation
They are two names for the same activity
Co-creation is with suppliers, collaboration with users
test.why: PRINCE2 describes co-creation as a specific form of collaboration (manual 3.3).

whyNot.1: This reverses the relationship: collaboration is the wider idea.
whyNot.2: Co-creation is narrower: it concerns users and key influencers designing products and ways of working.
whyNot.3: Co-creation specifically involves users and key influencers, not only suppliers.
